notes: Mode-A contract eval for the DIET-lane podcast takeaway summarizer (S11; signals.takeaway). Each case supplies a show name + episode title + raw RSS description and asserts the LLM returns: (1) non-empty text, (2) ≤ 400 chars, (3) no verbatim repetition of RSS marketing language that was explicitly flagged as disallowed. The grader scores recall against a set of required investment keywords — the model must surface at least one named company/fund/metric/catalyst from the description. The eval is a CONTRACT check (does the output satisfy the prompt's stated constraints?) not a quality judge (which phrasing is best?), so it is deterministic and requires no judge layer. Bump the prompt version tag in _build_prompt and re-run whenever the prompt template changes materially.

cases.title: David Velez — Building NU Into Latin America's Largest Digital Bank
cases.raw_body: Tune in this week as Patrick O'Shaughnessy sits down with David Velez, founder and CEO of NU Holdings (NYSE: NU), to discuss why Latin America's credit card penetration remains below 30%, how NIM expansion held at 18% even as funding costs rose, and what the path to 150 million customers looks like. Plus: Velez shares why regulatory capital buffers give NU room to accelerate Mexico.

cases.title: NVIDIA's Blackwell Ramp and the AI Infrastructure Supercycle
cases.raw_body: Brad Gerstner and Bill Gurley are back to break down NVIDIA's Q2 earnings beat — revenue of $30B vs $28.6B consensus, data-center growing 154% YoY — and whether Blackwell GPU supply constraints ease by Q4. They also debate the hyperscaler capex cycle: does $600B in combined AWS/Azure/GCP CapEx guidance signal a durable cycle or a catch-up spike?

cases.title: Meta's Year of Efficiency — One Year Later
cases.raw_body: Ben Thompson revisits Meta's Year of Efficiency: headcount -21% from 87,000 to 69,000, operating margin expanding from 25% to 41%, and Family DAP reaching 3.27 billion. Thompson examines whether Zuckerberg's focus on AI infrastructure (CapEx guide $37-40B) risks reversing the efficiency gains, and what Llama's open-weight strategy means for the ad-tech moat.
